incidents.victim: Stark Industries hosting infrastructure (MIRhosting / WorkTitans / the.hosting)
incidents.attacker: Russia — state-linked influence and DDoS operations (disrupted by Dutch authorities)
incidents.vector: Dutch FIOD arrested co-owners and seized 800+ servers used by Russia-linked actors for DDoS, proxy/anonymity services and influence operations across the EU.
incidents.impact: Two operators charged with sanctions violations; servers and laptops seized in Enschede, Almere, Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk. Networks were the most-used in pro-Russian DDoS attacks against Danish government bodies during Denmark's November 2025 municipal elections.

incidents.victim: German university hospitals (Cologne, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Ulm, Mannheim) via billing provider Unimed
incidents.vector: Third-party supply chain compromise: attackers breached external billing service provider Unimed in mid-April, accessing patient data handled on behalf of multiple university hospitals.
incidents.impact: Approximately 30,000 patients affected at Cologne, 54,000 at Freiburg, 11,000 at Heidelberg, 1,600 at Ulm; names, addresses, treating physicians, and in hundreds of cases diagnosis/treatment and bank/payment data exposed. Hospitals halted data transfers and are considering legal action.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense and telecoms organizations in the U.S., Israel, UAE and Middle East
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing recruitment lures (fake job portals, video conferencing installers) impersonating global air carriers, with DLL sideloading and AppDomainManager hijacking to deploy six new RAT variants in two malware families (MiniUpdate, MiniJunk V2).
incidents.impact: Coordinated Iran-nexus espionage campaigns timed to the regional conflict that began Feb 28, 2026; C2 routed through dedicated Azure-hosted domains to evade detection.

incidents.victim: Jacob Butler / KimWolf botnet (operator arrested in Canada)
incidents.vector: IoT botnet enslaved millions of digital photo frames, web cameras and other devices; rented to other cybercriminals and used to launch record-setting DDoS attacks up to ~30 Tbps.
incidents.impact: U.S. extradition warrant unsealed; Butler charged with operating the Kimwolf botnet which issued 25,000+ attack commands. Some victims reported losses exceeding $1M; attacks also targeted DoD IP ranges. Follows March 19 international seizure of Kimwolf, Aisuru, JackSkid and Mossad infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Supply chain compromise of an employee's device via a malicious VS Code extension, granting unauthorized access to internal code repositories.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800 internal repositories accessed; source code advertised for sale at $50,000 on a cybercrime forum with a threat to leak. GitHub says customer data was not affected; critical credentials rotated. Part of TeamPCP's cascading supply chain campaign that also hit TanStack, Trivy, LiteLLM, Mistral, UiPath, OpenAI and the European Commission.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a Salesforce-hosted system used to store franchisee documents; consistent with ShinyHunters' broader SaaS data-theft campaign.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses and Social Security numbers of franchisees exposed; breach discovered April 8 and disclosed to Maine, Vermont and Massachusetts regulators. 7-Eleven has nearly 10,000 U.S. franchise stores.

incidents.victim: SignSpaceCloud / Fox Tempest malware-signing-as-a-service (disrupted by Microsoft)
incidents.vector: Threat actor abused Microsoft Artifact Signing using hundreds of fake accounts to obtain code-signing certificates, then resold them on signspace[.]cloud to ransomware and malware operators.
incidents.impact: Microsoft sued and seized infrastructure; service generated millions of dollars and supplied certificates to Rhysida, INC, Qilin and Akira ransomware operators among others.

incidents.vector: CISA contractor published a public GitHub repository named 'Private-CISA' containing 844MB of sensitive data including AWS GovCloud keys, SAML certificates, plaintext passwords and an RSA private key for a CISA-IT GitHub app; commit logs show built-in secret scanning was deliberately disabled.
incidents.impact: Repository was public from Nov 13, 2025 until removal on May 14, 2026. Exposed credentials included still-valid keys with full read access across CISA-IT repos and ability to hijack CI/CD pipelines. Lawmakers Hassan, Thompson and Ramirez demanded briefings; CISA still working to invalidate keys a week after notification.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations across North America, Australia and the UK (Microsoft 365 / Okta tenants)
incidents.vector: Voice phishing of employees on personal cellphones impersonating IT help desk, combined with adversary-in-the-middle credential and MFA capture against subdomain-based lookalike SSO portals; followed by Python/PowerShell scripts using session cookies and Microsoft Graph to mass-exfiltrate SharePoint and OneDrive content.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations targeted since early 2026; in one case attackers downloaded over a million files from a single victim's SharePoint/OneDrive. Extortion demands open in the millions, often dropping to low six figures; escalation tactics include Gmail spam floods, threatening voicemails to executives and swatting of company personnel.

incidents.victim: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller / Manager customers (federal agencies and enterprises)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — state-sponsored espionage group (tracked as UAT-8616)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, a CVSS 10 authentication bypass that lets unauthenticated remote attackers impersonate a trusted router and gain administrative access; UAT-8616 then adds SSH keys, modifies NETCONF and escalates to root. Concurrent widespread exploitation of February CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122 chain by 10+ separate clusters deploying XenShell, Godzilla, Behinder, AdaptixC2, Sliver and XMRig.
incidents.impact: CISA added CVE-2026-20182 to KEV and ordered all federal agencies to patch by Sunday May 17; Cisco confirms exploitation across on-premises, cloud and FedRAMP deployments. Affected controllers manage routing for entire SD-WAN fabrics, giving attackers position to reroute traffic, intercept communications and push malicious configurations.

incidents.victim: Pierre & Vacances, Belambra and Gîtes de France
incidents.vector: Intrusion details undisclosed; customer data subsequently put up for sale online by the same individual on cybercrime forums.
incidents.impact: Three French holiday booking sites breached with data offered for sale by a single actor.

incidents.victim: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision) — North American factories
incidents.vector: Likely SEO-poisoning and malicious installers impersonating legitimate IT tools (AnyDesk, WinSCP, Cisco AnyConnect) based on Nitrogen's prior tradecraft; double-extortion ransomware operation.
incidents.impact: Cyberattack disrupted multiple North American facilities and forced employees in a Wisconsin plant to revert to pen-and-paper. Nitrogen claims theft of 8TB and 11M+ files including documentation referencing Intel, Apple, Google, Dell, Nvidia, AMD, JPMorgan Chase, HPE and Tencent. Factories resuming normal production.

incidents.vector: Cross-chain bridge exploitation (specific technique not disclosed in source).

incidents.victim: Transit Finance and TAC cross-chain platforms
incidents.vector: Exploitation of legacy smart contracts (four-year-old contract at Transit Finance; TON blockchain contract at TAC) on the same day.
incidents.impact: $1.9M stolen from Transit Finance and $2.8M from TAC; Transit Finance pledged to compensate users.

incidents.victim: TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, OpenAI (and ~400 packages across npm/PyPI)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply chain worm (TeamPCP / 'Mini Shai-Hulud')
incidents.vector: Self-propagating supply chain worm spreading via compromised npm/PyPI packages, stealing developer credentials, API keys, cloud secrets and cryptocurrency wallets; source code released on Breached[.]st with a $10,000 bounty for largest follow-on attack.
incidents.impact: Compromised the TanStack React framework and propagated to almost 400 packages including libraries at Mistral and UiPath; OpenAI rotated code-signing certificates after two employee devices were affected. Worm release expected to spawn copycat campaigns.

incidents.victim: CB Financial Services, Inc. (Pennsylvania community bank)
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed in the SEC filing.
incidents.impact: Filed Form 8-K Item 1.05 disclosing a material cybersecurity incident with reporting period May 7, 2026; further details not provided in the initial filing.

incidents.victim: City of Arcadia, California (mayor Eileen Wang)
incidents.vector: PRC officials directed Wang and co-conspirator Yaoning 'Mike' Sun via WeChat to publish pre-written pro-PRC propaganda articles on a Chinese-language 'news' website (U.S. News Center), coordinated with a high-level PRC intelligence figure.
incidents.impact: Arcadia mayor charged with acting as illegal agent of the PRC; agreed to plead guilty (10-year max). Co-conspirator already serving 4 years. Highlights covert PRC influence in U.S. local politics.

incidents.victim: RXNT (healthcare prescription software, used by U.S. Congress)
incidents.vector: Intrusion into RXNT systems in March 2026; specific vector not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Patient data stolen, including records of U.S. members of Congress who use RXNT for prescriptions. Company notified authorities on the final day allowed under U.S. health privacy laws.
